followup_rationale: No public follow-up is proposed. Exact optimal capacity and finite-block implementations are natural targets, but this review supplies neither a new converse mechanism nor a concrete coding construction that meets the requested high bar for a worthwhile research proposal.
key_boundaries: The rate is asymptotic over many independent resource copies and allows collective quantum decoding inside a receiver’s laboratory. It is not a one-copy advantage, a finite-block performance guarantee or an explicit practical family of codebooks.
The theorem gives a capacity lower bound. It does not prove that 3/2 + h₂(1/4) is the optimal LOCC capacity, characterize every achievable rate pair or rule out better protocols.
The error criterion is uniform average error over independent messages. Zero-error and maximal-error coding are not established.

The ownership and routing are fixed: each independent sender sends one qubit per copy to their own receiver, and receiver operations are local across A₁B₁ : A₂B₂. There is no sender message disclosure, feedback to senders, additional shared entanglement or quantum communication between receivers.

The two-bit calculation when both receivers immediately use Bell measurements concerns that particular one-copy measurement and input ensemble. It is not a converse bound for arbitrary one-copy LOCC strategies.

Bell forwarding and multiple-access dense coding have earlier precedents. The claimed addition is the specific retained-quantum-output channel and its achievable region for this W₄ problem, using Winter’s established coding theorem. This bounded comparison does not certify worldwide first priority, formal proof verification or completed human peer review.
